Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-platform/rules/service-registry.md + none

Read: card #31112 (body and all 20 comments, the slice-6 claim 6735852486 and dev report 6736276885 included), PR #31879 body, file list and the net diff against `main` at 3f0e3ace (2 files: the rules file, 2 lines changed; one new changeset), the check-runs on the head, and in the live tree `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`, `realtime-service.ts`, `cache-service.ts`, `objectql-engine.ts`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` and `engine.ts`, `packages/services/service-realtime/src/realtime-service-plugin.ts` and `in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts`, `packages/spec/scripts/check-skill-examples.ts`, `packages/spec/package.json`, `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, `skills/objectstack-platform/references/plugin-development.md`, `skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json`, and the three platform files on `main`. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head at record time: every concluded run is success or skipped (Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, every Lint job, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards). `Type Check · consumer gates` (the lint.yml job `typecheck-consumers`, which runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples`) has concluded: success. Still in progress at the last read: Test Core (1/8) and (2/8), which this prose-only diff cannot move.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set change: the diff touches no schema, no zod, no runtime code, no gate. Right.
- Public surface moved: the published skill bundle `@objectstack/skills` (`packages/skills`) ships a changed `rules/service-registry.md`, two example lines. Right, and the changeset names it.
- Basic Usage, L113: `db` is annotated `IDataEngine` and now calls `db.find('account')`. `IDataEngine.find(objectName: string, query?: EngineQueryOptions, options?: BaseEngineOptions): Promise of any[]` (data-engine.ts:401); the result then feeds `cache.set('accounts', result)`, and `ICacheService.set of T(key: string, value: T, ttl?: number)` (cache-service.ts:43) takes it. The concrete service behind the `objectql` key is `ObjectQLPlugin`'s `this.ql` (plugin.ts:852), `class ObjectQL implements IObjectQLEngine` (engine.ts:451), and `IObjectQLEngine extends IDataEngine` (objectql-engine.ts:298), so `find('account')` is true against the annotation and against the runtime. The old `db.object('account').find()` compiled only against the concrete class (`ObjectQL.object(name): ObjectRepository`, engine.ts:10274) and never against the annotated contract (TS2339); the sibling reference `plugin-development.md:103` uses the same `IDataEngine` annotation, so the file now agrees with it. Right.
- Optional Services, L126: `realtime` is annotated `IRealtimeService`; `publish(event: RealtimeEventPayload): Promise of void` (realtime-service.ts:100), and `RealtimeEventPayload` requires `type: string`, `payload: Record of string to unknown`, `timestamp: string` (ISO 8601) with `object?` optional (realtime-service.ts:19-28). The new call passes exactly the three required keys and awaits the promise. The runtime `realtime` key is registered by `realtime-service-plugin.ts:77` with `InMemoryRealtimeAdapter implements IRealtimeService` (in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts:75), so the shape is true against the runtime too. `data` is a free name in the block before and after, as in every other block of the file. Right.
- Teaching unchanged beyond truth: Basic Usage still teaches "resolve services in start() and use them"; Optional Services still teaches "try getService, degrade in catch". Neither fix adds a rule, removes one, or changes the ❌/✅ contrast. Right.
- The 0/40 finding holds. On `main` the three files carry 9 + 15 + 16 = 40 column-0 `ts`/`typescript` fences and no `os:check` marker. Every one of them either names `ctx`, `PluginContext`, `Plugin`, `kernel`, `ServiceLifecycle` or `LiteKernel` from `@objectstack/core`, or is a bare method fragment (plugin-lifecycle.md L156 `async destroy()` on `this`, TS1434 at top level). The skills surface of `check-skill-examples.ts` compiles under `resolutionDir: SPEC_DIR` with `selfPackages: [SPEC_DIR]` (L558-563); `packages/spec/package.json` depends on `zod` and `pg-connection-string` only, so `@objectstack/core` does not resolve (TS2307); spec's own `PluginContext` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin.zod.ts:55`, an alias of `PluginContextData`) is a different shape with no `hook`, `getService` or `registerService`. No wrapper of a few lines can mark any of them. Right.
- Token ratchet: the CEILINGS row for the file is 2331 (`check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:918`) and the diff does not touch it; the dev reports 1764 to 1777. The ratchet step (lint.yml `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`) sits in a concluded green job. Right.
- `check:skill-examples` count: no block gains a mark, so 343 before and after; the reverse check is not owed. Right.
- Skill links: `check-skill-links.mjs:417` pins this file's moved-registry anchors; the diff changes no link. Right.
- PR body and dev report account: both match the tree (two lines, no mark, changeset only). Judged from the tree, not the account.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31112-platform-service-registry-examples.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the PR body. The diff publishes a prose correction inside a published skill file and nothing else, so patch is the level, exactly as the card's Acceptance section fixes it for every slice and as slices 1 to 5 wrote it. The changeset body's claims (two examples, which contracts, 0 of 40 marked before and after, why) each check against the tree. Right.

Clause-②: no — right. The diff narrows no declared capability and declares no new one; plain `no`, not `no (narrowing)`.

Dev-report `deviations`:
- "check:skill-examples is not in the derived list; run by hand" — answered: CI runs it in `Type Check · consumer gates` (lint.yml `typecheck-consumers`), which concluded success on this head.
- "seat ruling (thread, 08:53Z): no fragment/core note lines; file surface narrowed to service-registry.md plus one changeset" — answered: the diff matches the ruling (one rules file, one changeset, no note lines added, plugin-lifecycle.md and plugin-hooks.md untouched).
- "no ceiling raised or lowered" — answered: the CEILINGS map is not in the diff.
- "default tier, no Fable build" — answered: this record is the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review the claim amendment 6724423900 promised in its place.

Dev-report `out_of_scope_findings`:
- "service-registry.md L222 and L232 (the optional-service pair) also call realtime.publish('event', data) with two arguments · carrier: seat" — escalated, not accepted as out of scope: see F1 below.
- "platform plugin examples stay outside check:skill-examples while it resolves only @objectstack/spec · carrier: none" — answered: agreed and not for this PR. The checker's own header (`check-skill-examples.ts` L386-413) says a page needing something neither surface carries is a new surface question, and spec depending on core would invert the direction the surface models. A follow-up card, if the seat wants one; not a flag on this head.

`open_questions`: none in the report. No ruling on the card is contradicted by the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-platform/rules/service-registry.md` against the card's eval set (`config-plugins-ops.json`, eval 1 expects a plugin whose `init(ctx)` calls `ctx.registerService('audit', ...)` and `ctx.hook(...)`; no eval asserts on the two changed lines) and against the contracts it teaches on `main`:

- Both changed lines hold against the cited code, sentence by sentence (section ① above). Tried to break them: `find('account')` with no query is allowed (`query?`); `set` takes any value type; `publish` refuses a missing `timestamp` or `payload`, and the new literal supplies both; `object` is optional and omitted; `await` on a `Promise of void` is well typed. Nothing breaks.

- F1 · should-fix · L222 and L232 (the "No Error Handling for Optional Service" ❌/✅ pair). Both halves still call `realtime.publish('event', data)` with two arguments: the same method on the same `realtime` service whose call shape L126 corrects, one hundred lines below it in the same file. Against the contract and the runtime (`InMemoryRealtimeAdapter implements IRealtimeService`) that call is refused. The pair's lesson is try/catch around `getService`, not the publish shape, so correcting the arity to the one-argument payload blunts nothing; left as is, the file teaches two shapes for one call, and the ✅ half is the one an agent copies. `getService('realtime')` with no type argument infers `T` as `unknown`, so the block would not compile either way, but the teaching is what is read. The pair sits inside the claim's file surface, the ratchet has 554 tokens of headroom, and the PR exists to make this file's examples call the contracts they annotate. A fix moves the head and earns a delta review; it does not change what any rule teaches.

- F2 · nit · L126 adds `await` inside the try whose catch logs "Realtime service not available — skipping", so a rejected `publish` is now reported as unavailability. The contract returns a promise, so awaiting it is right and the un-awaited call was a floating promise; the misattribution is the pre-existing shape of the pattern (the ✅ half at L229-236 scopes its try the same way) and has no effect on the contract. Accepted deviation, or folded into F1's edit if the seat wants the publish outside the try.

- Observation, pre-existing, outside the hunks, not graded for this PR: L7 says the context "provides three core methods" and the block below lists four; `replaceService` in `packages/core/src/types.ts:48` is `replaceService of T(name, implementation: T)` where L17 writes `instance: any`. For a later edit of this file.

Nothing in the diff implements or enforces the rule (no gate, no validator, no schema), so there is no implementing file to judge; the changeset is release metadata and is covered in ②.
